bash-scripting-sr3-07.reason: Weak card (strawman false side), rewritten rather than dropped: dropping sr3-02, sr3-06, sr3-07 and sr3-09 would leave r3 with 8 cards. This uses the verifier's replacement on the documented :- versus negative-offset trap. Confirmed on man7 Parameter Expansion: 'a negative offset must be separated from the colon by at least one space to avoid being confused with the :- expansion'. Bash 5.3.20 gives [abcdef] for ${x:-2} and [ef] for ${x: -2}. (final: keep)
bash-scripting-sr3-07.statement: With x=abcdef, Bash expands ${x:-2} to ef, the last two characters of x.
bash-scripting-sr3-07.explanation: Written as ${x:-2}, this is the :- default-value operator; x is set and non-null, so the result is abcdef. A negative substring offset must be separated from the colon by a space, as in ${x: -2}.
bash-scripting-sr3-07.misconception: ${x:-2} is a negative substring offset that counts from the end of the value.

bash-scripting-sr7-05.reason: Duplicate of sr9-08 (list status is the last command's status), rewritten rather than dropped: dropping sr7-04, sr7-05 and sr7-10 would leave r7 at 3 true / 6 false. This uses the verifier's replacement, with the 'because its body never runs' clause removed (a negation and an answer-giving reason). Confirmed on man7 Compound Commands: 'The exit status of the while and until commands is the exit status of the last command executed in list-2, or zero if none was executed.' Bash 5.3.20 prints while=0. (final: keep)
bash-scripting-sr7-05.statement: Bash gives while false; do :; done an exit status of zero.
bash-scripting-sr7-05.explanation: A while or until loop returns the status of the last body command it ran, or zero when the body never ran, so the failed condition's status is discarded.

source.title: GNU Bash man page: Compound Commands (while and until)

bash-scripting-sr12-01.reason: Duplicate across decks (linux-command-line-sr7-03, 2>&1 before >), rewritten rather than dropped: dropping the four duplicates would leave r12 with 8 cards at 3 true / 5 false. This uses the verifier's {varname} replacement. Confirmed on man7 REDIRECTION: 'the shell allocates a file descriptor greater than or equal to 10 and assigns it to varname'. Bash 5.3.20 gives fd=10. (final: keep)
bash-scripting-sr12-01.statement: For exec {fd}>log, Bash assigns fd a descriptor number of 10 or higher.
bash-scripting-sr12-01.explanation: A {varname} word in place of a descriptor number makes Bash allocate a descriptor of at least 10 and store its number in the variable, so scripts avoid hard-coded numbers.

bash-scripting-sr12-04.reason: Source problem: man7 bash(1) does not say that a redirection on a compound command covers the commands inside it. The Bash Reference Manual's Compound Commands section does: 'Any redirections associated with a compound command apply to all commands within that compound command unless explicitly overridden.' gnu.org refused connections today, so I confirmed this sentence in the released Bash 5.3 bash.info shipped with 5.3.20. Statement and explanation are unchanged. (final: fixed)
bash-scripting-sr12-04.statement: Bash applies the >out redirection in { printf a; printf b; } >out to both printf commands.
bash-scripting-sr12-04.explanation: A redirection attached to a compound command such as a brace group applies to every command inside it unless one overrides it, so both printf outputs go to out.

bash-scripting-sr10-04.reason: tell: in r10, 'exits before printf x' appeared only on true cards (scan tell 1). The fact (errexit ignores a pipeline inverted with !) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Bash 5.3.20 prints x. (final: keep)
bash-scripting-sr10-04.statement: With set -e, Bash exits before printf x in ! true; printf x.
bash-scripting-sr10-04.explanation: Bash ignores errexit for a pipeline whose status is inverted with !. This script therefore continues to printf x.
bash-scripting-sr10-04.misconception: A negated pipeline's failed overall status triggers errexit.

source.title: GNU Bash man page: set builtin: errexit

bash-scripting-sr10-05.reason: tell: this moves a second false card into the 'exits before printf x' frame, which balances scan tell 1. The fact (errexit is ignored throughout a function called as an if condition) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Bash 5.3.20 prints x. (final: keep)
bash-scripting-sr10-05.statement: With set -e, Bash exits before printf x in f(){ false; printf x; }; if f; then :; fi.
bash-scripting-sr10-05.explanation: Calling f as an if condition makes Bash ignore errexit throughout that function body. The false is followed by printf x.
bash-scripting-sr10-05.misconception: A tested function call retains errexit handling for failures inside its body.

source.title: GNU Bash man page: set builtin: errexit

bash-scripting-sr2-01.reason: tell: as an ordering word, 'before' was 1 true to 6 false across the deck (scan tell 2). This rewords the true card's ordering claim to use 'before'. The fact (word splitting comes before pathname expansion) and the answer (true) are unchanged. (final: fixed)
bash-scripting-sr2-01.statement: With x='a *.cfg', Bash splits unquoted $x into two words before applying pathname expansion to them.
bash-scripting-sr2-01.explanation: Word splitting comes before pathname expansion, so the unquoted value first becomes the words a and *.cfg, and Bash then matches *.cfg against filenames.

bash-scripting-sr8-12.reason: tell: the 'With X off' option premise was 1 true to 5 false (scan tell 3). This removes the premise from one false card. The fact (local - restores only set options, not shopt) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Bash 5.3.20 shows nullglob on after f. (final: keep)
bash-scripting-sr8-12.statement: For f(){ local -; shopt -s nullglob; }, Bash returns nullglob to its earlier off state when f ends.
bash-scripting-sr8-12.explanation: local - restores options changed through set. This shopt change persists, so nullglob remains enabled after f returns.
bash-scripting-sr8-12.misconception: local - restores shopt settings together with set options.
